Places copied with schema: keys. A GeoShape polygon ("lon lat" ring) is replaced by its bounding box as schema:box ("minLat minLon maxLat maxLon"), since the CDIF geoShape shape accepts box or line, not polygon.

The source DefinedTerm is reduced to name (from its description) and termCode; its enumerated term sets are dropped. A bare string becomes a DefinedTerm name.

PropertyValues copied with schema: keys. The source spatial-reference entries carry only propertyID and value, so schema:name (required by the CDIF discovery shape) is derived from the last segment of propertyID.
Plain schema:PropertyValue (discovery level, not cdi:InstanceVariable). Names and descriptions are whitespace-stripped; an entry with no name is dropped.

Kept on the dataset with schema: keys. OPEN QUESTION: the other CDIF converters put the catalog on the catalog record (schema:subjectOf), where schema:includedInDataCatalog describes the metadata record.
Reduced to bare {@id} references, so the cited works are not pulled into the dataset-completeness shapes. Items with no @id are dropped.

The source lists download URL strings. Each http(s) URL becomes a schema:DataDownload with contentUrl, and encodingFormat from the URL's format= query parameter (mapped to a MIME type where known). Placeholders such as "TBD" are dropped.

The source's about Events each carry a potentialAction. The one with object, instrument and result (the real ETL step: curl, wget, ...) becomes one [prov:Activity, schema:Action] (cdifProv); the "Pseudo Code" / "TODO" placeholder Event is dropped. --no-provenance drops both.
Prefixed "ETL: " (e.g. "ETL: wget").
Copied as is.

Wrapped in prov:used (the cdifProv instrument pattern). The source tool has no name, so one is made from its featureList: "GDSC ETL tools (<command>)".
The source result is an inline Dataset (the SQL export); it is replaced by an {@id} reference to the record's own dataset, which is what the activity generated.
